content_sections.body_text: ‘I was walking to class when rain started. First, I opened my umbrella. Then the wind broke it. I made a decision to wait in the library. Finally, the rain stopped and I left.’ The background, events, and ending form one clear sequence.
content_sections.title: Read a connected account

content_sections.body_text: Underline first, then, and finally; number the events 1–4. Circle made a decision: English conventionally combines make with decision. Notice that was walking gives the background while started and broke move the account forward.
content_sections.title: Notice order and combination

content_sections.body_text: Relative prominence marks the new or contrasting information: ‘I waited in the LIBRARY, not the café.’ Make LIBRARY clearer and stronger than nearby words. Change the place to HOME; the strongest word changes because the intended contrast changes.
content_sections.title: Signal information focus

content_sections.body_text: Replace rain with one problem and library with one solution. Plan four events, include first/then/finally and make a decision, then retell without reading. Check: order is recoverable, background differs from completed events, the lexical combination is intact, and one focused word is clearly prominent.
content_sections.title: Transform, retell, verify
